Study for the painting “Intake”

Bridget Riley’s black poster-colour study of 1964: wavy black and white bands that tighten into one corner.

Source
V&A: Study for the painting “Intake”, CIRC.237-1965
Creator
Bridget Riley
Made
1964
Style
Op art (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Vibrating, fluid, high-contrast
Evidence
Downloaded and inspected the V&A image of its copy, CIRC.237-1965 (1552 × 1600 px), in a scratchpad. No image is stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A catalogues the drawing with the style “Op Art”: pencil and black poster colour on paper, 26.3 × 29.4 cm, acquired by the V&A Circulation Department in 1965. V&A.

The V&A’s general Riley text also says she designed the Woolmark logo while at an advertising agency. That claim conflicts with the usual attribution of the logo to Franco Grignani, and it is not repeated here as fact. V&A.

Observed

  • Alternating black and white bands run from the lower left toward the top right corner inside a square.
  • At the lower left the bands are broad and gently curved; toward the top right they narrow, bend more, and converge.
  • The bands are flat and hard-edged, painted in solid black with no tone.
  • A narrow grey mount shows around the square.

Why it belongs

The study isolates the core op device of the style: a stripe field that changes width by steps until the eye reads movement and depth.

Its hand-painted scale shows that Riley’s effects were planned in small studies before the large paintings.

Borrow

Run a stripe field diagonally and let it converge into one corner to create a strong direction.

Change stripe width and curvature together, not separately, so that the field seems to turn in space.
